The two DXC panes should not compile the first arm. They report an internal compiler error
rather than a diagnostic about modifying a const object, and exit with a failure status; read
the error text in each pane rather than the exit code alone, because the wording differs
between the two DXC versions.

Obj is a file-scope object, so it is implicitly const and lives in $Globals. Set() is not
marked const and writes a member.

The last pane is the control: the same shader with -DCONTROL_MUTABLE, which makes the object
static and therefore mutable, so there is no const violation. It compiles. Compare it with the
pane above it, which is the same compiler on the same source without that define. Without the
control, a Clang diagnostic here would not be distinguishable from Clang failing on the shader
for reasons of its own.

The shader is the maintainer's compute restating of the issue, taken from the Compiler Explorer
link already in the thread, with the control arm added behind the define. The vertex-shader
form in the issue body behaves the same way locally; compute is used here so the Clang panes
can participate, since its pixel and vertex backends cannot lower signature I/O.
